draft.title: The geography of Sparta
card: Sparta lay in Laconia, in the south of the Peloponnese. It sat in the valley of the Eurotas river, where the soil was fertile.
Mountains ringed the valley: the Taygetus range to the west and the Parnon range to the east. They made Sparta hard to attack and cut it off from other regions.
Sparta conquered Messenia, its neighbour to the west, beyond the Taygetus mountains. This gave Sparta more farmland.
Fertile land supported a food supply, and the mountains gave protection. Sparta also had to keep control of the large territory it had taken.
draft.remember: A fertile valley, mountain barriers and conquered Messenia shaped Sparta's strength and its worries.

a.q: Which feature of Sparta's geography helped protect it from attack?
opts: Mountains that ringed the Eurotas valley
A long coastline open to trade
Wide plains that let armies move quickly
Messenia lying to the north of the city
a.why: The Taygetus and Parnon ranges surrounded the valley and made an attack on Sparta difficult. Wide plains would have helped an enemy, not protected Sparta.
a.clue: Think about what surrounded the valley.

b.q: Why did Sparta's conquest of Messenia matter to the Spartans?
opts: It gave Sparta a route to the Eurotas river
It moved Sparta's city into Messenia
It removed the mountains around Sparta
b.why: Messenia lay beyond the Taygetus mountains and its conquest added farmland to what Sparta already had in Laconia. Sparta already stood on the Eurotas, so the conquest did not give it the river.
b.clue: Ask what the conquered land could be used for.

a.best: Mountains that ringed the Eurotas valley
